facts.text: Redford was founded around 1876 as El Polvo, Spanish for “the dust,” and its first post office opened in 1911.
The town sits along the Rio Grande on Farm Road 170, about sixteen miles southeast of Presidio in Presidio County.
A historic church inn in Redford, built in 1920, still offers queen‑size beds, a communal kitchen, and a lounge overlooking the Rio Grande.
The gravesite of Esequiel Hernández, a famed Mexican‑American soldier, is a well‑known landmark in the community.
Redford’s name change from El Polvo to its current form reflects the town’s evolution from a dusty frontier stop to a settled community.
The town’s historic register listing includes a 104‑year‑old building with hardwood floors that once served as a general store.
